title: Large-scale SSE/WSS streaming load harness with adaptive token pacing and regression gates
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a horizontally scalable load-testing harness that emulates realistic streaming chat traffic over SSE and WebSocket (WSS) at token-level fidelity. The harness will exercise KV-cache warming, prefix caching, and bursty session churn to validate p95/p99 tail latency, tokens/sec throughput, and regression detection for streaming completions. The overall goal is to provide reproducible stress scenarios that match production shapes and to gate runtime changes in CI via statistical regression detection.
design_notes: Key design constraints: 1) Keep per-client state light so we can scale to tens of thousands of concurrent simulated sessions. 2) Support both SSE and WSS protocols with identical token pacing semantics. 3) Pluggable persona profiles (short/long context, frequent vs rare completions) and KV-awareness so clients can prewarm relevant keys. 4) Adaptive token pacing that adjusts per-connection emission to mimic user typing and backpressure caused by server-side latency. 5) Deterministic seeding option to reproduce runs for debugging.
instrumentation: Emit high-cardinality metrics at both client and server probe points: tokens_sent, tokens_received, stream_open_ms, first_token_time_ms, per-token_latency_ms distribution, p50/p90/p95/p99 token latency, connection_retries, kv_cache_hit_rate, payload_size_bytes, stream_errors. All metrics are tagged by protocol (sse|wss), persona, tenant_sim_id, and run_id. Traces for slow sessions sampled at higher probability and correlated with run_id.
metrics: Primary: tokens/sec (global and per-tenant), p95 token latency, p99 token latency. Secondary: stream success rate, reconnect rate, KV cache hit rate, end-to-end completion throughput. Derived: cost_estimate_per_million_tokens (using current price-model), effective_concurrency.
regression_strategy: Use control and experiment windows with bootstrap-based confidence intervals on p95 and tokens/sec. Default test: non-parametric bootstrap to compute 95% CI for difference in p95 and in tokens/sec; trigger a CI regression if experiment p95 > control p95 by >= 20% and CI excludes zero, or tokens/sec drops by >= 15% and CI excludes zero. For high-noise scenarios, fallback to Mann–Whitney U with multiple-run aggregation. Maintain an evolving baseline from weekly synthesis runs.
alerting_and_gating: Integrate with CI pipeline: harness produces an artifacts bundle (metrics CSV, histogram snapshots, run_id). CI job runs statistical detector; failures block merges and open an automated rollback candidate. Create Grafana dashboards and an Alerting policy that posts to PagerDuty for severity-high regressions. Slack summary with run digest and top-10 slow sessions is produced automatically.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for pacing algorithms and persona synthesis. 2) Small-scale local smoke run (100 sessions) to validate protocol parity. 3) Staging-run that targets a known canary runtime (10k sessions) and verifies metrics tagflow. 4) Weekly baseline runs against a pinned model/instance type. 5) Synthetic chaos scenarios: 5–10% random connection churn, simulated 500ms upstream host latency, KV-cache cold-start windows. 6) Repro runs using deterministic seeding to trace failures to code/PRs.
ci_integration: Produce a single JSON/CSV artifact with run metadata (run_id, git_ref, docker_image, node_count, persona_mix) uploaded to S3/gcs. Provide a lightweight 'regression-check' binary used in CI that downloads artifact and baseline, runs the statistical detector, and returns non-zero on fail. Job lives in ci/runtime/regression-check.yml and is optional gated on runtime changes and PR size > 300 LOC.
ops_runbook: Runbook sections: 1) How to start an ad-hoc harness run in staging. 2) How to interpret p95/p99 histograms and identify KV-miss dominated tails. 3) Steps to extract top offender traces and associate with model shard or kernel. 4) Rollback triggers and runbook for bumping capacity or enabling temporary throttles. 5) Postmortem checklist when regression gate fails in CI.
risks_mitigation: Risk: harness itself causes non-linear load on control plane. Mitigation: rate-limited orchestrator, sharded workers that self-throttle, and a dry-run mode that validates client-side behavior without hitting runtime. Risk: false positives in noisy infra. Mitigation: require at least two independent runs with consistent effect before automatic rollback; human-in-loop review for borderline cases.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: prototype of adaptive pacing implemented and unit-tested
2026-02-20: SSE and WSS protocol parity verified in local harness
2026-02-28: integrated KV-prewarm hooks and added persona templates (customer_support, search_assist, code_completion)
2026-03-05: first staging run (12k sessions) completed; observed 18% p95 variance vs baseline — investigating trace samples
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can run 20k concurrent simulated streams (SSE + WSS mix configurable) while collecting required metrics with <5% instrumentation overhead. 2) Regression detector implemented and returns deterministic pass/fail for synthetic regressions injected in control experiments. 3) CI integration and dashboards wired; first CI gate run executed and documented. 4) Run artifacts retained per retention policy and reproducible via deterministic seeding.
notes_for_followups: Follow-ups: expand persona library with mobile vs desktop network profiles, add tenant-weighted fairness generator, export sample payload traces to paced storage for debugging, and tune bootstrap-sample size for noisy model releases.
short_summary: High-fidelity streaming load harness for SSE/WSS with adaptive token pacing, KV-aware prewarm, statistical regression detection, CI gating, and Grafana dashboards to protect runtime p95/token throughput SLAs.
